# Brand images

HACS and the Home Assistant frontend take an integration's icon from the
[home-assistant/brands](https://github.com/home-assistant/brands) repository, not from this
one. The images are ready in [`brands/`](../brands) — they just have to be submitted there.

`brands/icon.png` (256×256) and `brands/icon@2x.png` (512×512) are generated by
`scripts/make_brand_images.py`, so the mark is reproducible rather than a binary nobody can
change. It is a warm-to-cool sweep through white: the path the adaptive curve walks across a
day, which is the one idea the integration is about.

To finish the submission:

1. Fork `home-assistant/brands`.
2. Create `custom_integrations/better_lighting/`.
3. Copy `brands/icon.png` and `brands/icon@2x.png` into it.
4. Open a pull request.
5. Once it is **merged**, delete the `ignore: brands` line from
   `.github/workflows/validate.yaml`. Until then that check would fail, because it asks the
   brands repository whether the domain exists there — having the files locally is not enough.

Replacing the mark with something hand-drawn is entirely reasonable; nothing depends on it.
